thread.title: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is First Quadrant L P CA’s 2nd Largest Position

author: Jennifer Salazar
title: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) is First Quadrant L P CA’s 2nd Largest Position
text:
Posted by Jennifer Salazar on May 12th, 2018 // No Comments
First Quadrant L P CA lessened its stake in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 17.5% in the 4th quarter, according to its most recent Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The fund owned 817,578 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 173,629 shares during the quarter. Apple comprises approximately 2.6% of First Quadrant L P CA’s portfolio, making the stock its 2nd biggest position. First Quadrant L P CA’s holdings in Apple were worth $138,359,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other institutional investors also recently added to or reduced their stakes in AAPL. Oak Point Wealth Management purchased a new position in shares of Apple in the fourth quarter valued at $163,000. Crow Point Partners LLC increased its position in shares of Apple by 100.0% in the third quarter. Crow Point Partners LLC now owns 1,000 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $153,000 after buying an additional 500 shares in the last quarter. Interactive Financial Advisors purchased a new position in shares of Apple in the fourth quarter valued at $188,000. Home Federal Bank of Tennessee purchased a new position in shares of Apple in the fourth quarter valued at $217,000. Finally, JJJ Advisors Inc. purchased a new position in shares of Apple in the third quarter valued at $201,000. Institutional investors and hedge funds own 61.12% of the company’s stock. AAPL has been the topic of a number of analyst reports. Bank of America lowered Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating and increased their price objective for the company from $180.00 to $220.00 in a research note on Wednesday, January 17th. Cascend Securities increased their price objective on Apple from $200.00 to $220.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a research note on Monday, January 29th. Morgan Stanley reaffirmed a “buy” rating and set a $205.00 price objective (up previously from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a research note on Tuesday, January 23rd. Rosenblatt Securities reissued a “buy” rating and issued a $180.00 price target on shares of Apple in a research note on Friday, January 19th. Finally, Maxim Group raised their price target on Apple from $193.00 to $204.00 and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research note on Friday, January 12th. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have assigned a hold rating, thirty-three have given a buy rating and two have assigned a strong buy rating to the stock. The company presently has a consensus rating of “Buy” and an average price target of $204.00.
In other news, insider Philip W. Schiller sold 69,491 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction on Tuesday, April 3rd. The stock was sold at an average price of $166.42, for a total transaction of $11,564,692.22. The sale was disclosed in a document filed with the SEC, which is available through the SEC website . Also, insider Luca Maestri sold 39,122 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction on Friday, April 13th. The stock was sold at an average price of $174.66, for a total value of $6,833,048.52. Following the sale, the insider now directly owns 64,475 shares in the company, valued at $11,261,203.50. The disclosure for this sale can be found here . Insiders have sold 214,869 shares of company stock worth $37,493,244 over the last ninety days. 0.08% of the stock is owned by insiders.
Shares of Apple traded down $0.72, reaching $188.59, on Friday, MarketBeat reports. 26,167,293 shares of the company were exchanged, compared to its average volume of 36,315,044. The firm has a market capitalization of $950.67 billion, a PE ratio of 20.48, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.39 and a beta of 1.26. The company has a quick ratio of 1.37, a current ratio of 1.46 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. Apple has a fifty-two week low of $187.45 and a fifty-two week high of $190.06.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last announced its earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, topping analysts’ consensus estimates of $2.69 by $0.04. The company had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 39.97% and a net margin of 21.55%. Apple’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same period in the previous year, the firm earned $2.10 earnings per share. analysts expect that Apple will post 11.43 EPS for the current year.
The business also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Stockholders of record on Monday, May 14th will be given a dividend of $0.73 per share. The ex-dividend date of this dividend is Friday, May 11th. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. This represents a $2.92 dividend on an annualized basis and a dividend yield of 1.55%. Apple’s payout ratio is 27.36%.
Apple declared that its board has authorized a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to buyback $100.00 billion in outstanding shares. This buyback authorization allows the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares buyback plans are typically a sign that the company’s management believes its shares are undervalued.

Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers to consumers, and small and mid-sized businesses; and education, enterprise, and government customers worldwide.
